newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hogs $.50-$2 lower, ample supply -trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hogs $.50-$2 lower, ample supply -trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs traded $0.50 to $2.00 per cwt lower Wednesday, with ample numbers of hogs coming to market early and Tuesday's lower cash pork prices weighing on bids, livestock dealers said.
In Iowa and southern Minnesota, hogs traded from $53.00 to $54.00 per cwt at country points and $54.00 to $54.50 delivered to plants, sources there said.
Illinois hogs traded down $0.50 to $1.00 at $53.50 to $54.50 at country points and $55.00 at plants.

Indiana and Ohio hogs traded down $0.50 to $1.00. Indiana hogs sold at $53.00 at country points and $54.50 to $55.00 at plants and Ohio hogs from $51.00 to $52.00 at country points and $53.00 to $54.00 at plants, sources said.
Several major packers continue to operate reduced slaughter shifts because of poor operating margins. Sources said packers may return to full shifts Friday in place of a Saturday slaughter.
USDA reported pork cutout values fell $0.86 to $0.67 per cwt late Tuesday.
Iowa sources reported locally icy conditions, but said hog marketings should not greatly affect hog marketings.
